summary: The address, data and control buses, the registers used in the fetch-decode-execute cycle, and how clock speed, word length and bus width affect performance.

blocks.content: A set of parallel wires that **connects the CPU, main memory and input/output controllers**, made of three buses.

rows: The **memory address** (or I/O port) to be read or written
**Control and timing signals**: memory read, memory write, clock, interrupt request, bus request, reset

blocks.content:
flowchart LR
  CPU[CPU] -- address bus --> MEM[Main memory]
  CPU -- address bus --> IO[I/O controllers]
  CPU <-- data bus --> MEM
  CPU <-- data bus --> IO
  CPU <-. control bus .-> MEM
  CPU <-. control bus .-> IO
blocks.caption: Buses connecting the components

blocks.title: Registers
rows: Holds the **address of the next instruction**
Holds the address of the location to be read/written
Holds the data/instruction just read from or to be written to memory
Holds the instruction being decoded and executed

blocks.title: Fetch–decode–execute in register transfer notation
items: **MAR ← [PC]** — the address of the next instruction is copied to the MAR (sent along the address bus).
**PC ← [PC] + 1** — the PC is incremented to point to the following instruction.
**MDR ← [[MAR]]** — the instruction at that address is read into the MDR via the data bus (control bus: *memory read*).
**CIR ← [MDR]** — the instruction is copied to the CIR.
**Decode** — the control unit splits the instruction into **opcode** and **operand** and works out what to do.
**Execute** — the ALU or control unit carries it out (e.g. load, add, store, jump — a jump changes the PC).

blocks.content: Learn the notation exactly: square brackets `[ ]` mean **"the contents of"**. `[[MAR]]` = the contents of the address held in MAR.

rows: Higher → more instructions per second (limited by heat)
Number of bits the CPU processes as one unit (32, 64 bits)
Longer → larger numbers and more data per operation
Number of bits transferred at once
Wider → more data per transfer, fewer transfers
Wider → more memory can be addressed (2ⁿ locations)
More tasks in parallel (if software supports it)

blocks.content: Doubling the data bus width from 32 to 64 bits lets the CPU transfer **8 bytes instead of 4** in one bus cycle, so moving a block of data takes about **half as many** transfers.
